from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Text prompts turn into images via two main systems.",
            "CLIP understands the connection between text and images.",
            "Diffusion gradually creates images from static white noise."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The Image Synthesis Pipeline", lecture_lines)
        
        input_prompt = Text("Input Prompt", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        neural_pipeline = Rectangle(height=1.5, width=2.5, color="#ADD8E6", fill_opacity=0.3)
        pipeline_label = Text("Neural Pipeline", font_size=20, color="#ADD8E6").move_to(neural_pipeline.get_center())
        pipeline_group = VGroup(neural_pipeline, pipeline_label)
        arrow = Arrow(start=LEFT, end=RIGHT, color=WHITE).set_length(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.place_at_grid(input_prompt, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(input_prompt))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.place_at_grid(pipeline_group, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(pipeline_group))
        
        arrow.next_to(input_prompt, RIGHT)
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "CLIP maps text and images to shared vector space.",
            "Aligned vectors share similar directions, showing semantic similarity.",
            "Cosine similarity measures how close these vectors are."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("CLIP: Mapping Language to Visual Space", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define colors (B039)
        text_color = "#FFD700" # Gold
        image_color = "#00FFFF" # Cyan
        matrix_color = "#FF69B4" # HotPink
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # CLIP maps text and images to shared vector space.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(text_color)
        
        text_space = Circle(color=text_color, radius=0.5).set_fill(text_color, opacity=0.3)
        text_label = Text("Text Space", font_size=18, color=text_color)
        text_group = VGroup(text_space, text_label).arrange(DOWN)
        
        image_space = Circle(color=image_color, radius=0.5).set_fill(image_color, opacity=0.3)
        image_label = Text("Visual Space", font_size=18, color=image_color)
        image_group = VGroup(image_space, image_label).arrange(DOWN)
        
        self.place_at_grid(text_group, 'B4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(image_group, 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(text_group), FadeIn(image_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Aligned vectors share similar directions, showing semantic similarity.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(text_color)
        
        matrix_rect = Rectangle(color=matrix_color, width=2, height=1).set_fill(matrix_color, opacity=0.2)
        matrix_label = Text("CLIP Embedding", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        matrix_group = VGroup(matrix_rect, matrix_label)
        
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_group, 'C5', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Cosine similarity measures how close these vectors are.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(text_color)
        
        # Represent mapping with arrows
        arrow1 = Arrow(text_group.get_bottom(), matrix_group.get_top(), color=WHITE)
        arrow2 = Arrow(matrix_group.get_bottom(), image_group.get_top(), color=WHITE)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Diffusion adds noise to an image, destroying its structure.",
            "A neural network learns to predict this added noise.",
            "Reversing this process recovers the image from noise."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Diffusion Process: Math as an Artist", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        image_frame = Rectangle(width=2, height=2, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(image_frame, "C5", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        noise = Dot(point=self.grid["C5"], color="#808080", radius=0.1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.add(noise)
        self.play(Create(image_frame), FadeIn(noise))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        # Visualizing neural net prediction
        net_text = Text("Neural Network", font_size=18, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(net_text, "B5")
        self.play(Write(net_text))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Denoising
        self.play(noise.animate.set_color(WHITE), run_time=2)
        target = TargetMarker = Circle(radius=0.2, color=GREEN).set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(target, "C5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(target))
        
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):

        self.setup_layout("Guidance: Bridging Text and Noise", [

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis and Conclusion", [
            "Iterative denoising refines noise into a coherent image.",
            "The process uses 50 to 100 small steps.",
            "The final result is art born from noise."
        ])
        
        # Assets
        prompt_box = Rectangle(width=2, height=0.8, color=BLUE).add(Text("Prompt", font_size=18).move_to(ORIGIN))
        image_box = Rectangle(width=2, height=2, color=GREEN).add(Text("Image", font_size=18).move_to(ORIGIN))
        
        self.place_at_grid(prompt_box, 'B4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(image_box, 'D5', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(FadeIn(prompt_box), FadeIn(image_box))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        # Animate iterative refinement between Prompt and Image
        steps = VGroup(*[Dot(color=ORANGE).scale(0.5) for _ in range(3)])
        self.add(steps)
        for i, dot in enumerate(steps):
            dot.move_to(self.grid['B4'])
            self.play(dot.animate.move_to(self.grid['D5']), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(steps))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(image_box.animate.scale(1.2).set_color(WHITE), run_time=1.0)
        self.play(Indicate(image_box))
        
        # Terminal anchor icon (B007)
        target = Star(color=GREEN, fill_opacity=1).scale(0.2)
        target.move_to(self.grid['D5'])
        self.play(FadeIn(target))
        
        self.wait(2)
        self.play(FadeOut(self.lecture), FadeOut(self.title), FadeOut(prompt_box), FadeOut(image_box), FadeOut(target))

outline.topic: The Magic of Text-to-Image AI: Diffusion, CLIP, and the Math Behind the Art
outline.target_audience: University students with a basic background in linear algebra and probability.

sections.title: Introduction: The Image Synthesis Pipeline
sections.content: A 30-second overview of how text prompts transform into high-resolution images. Introduce the two pillars: CLIP (the 'Understanding' bridge) and Diffusion (the 'Creation' engine).
sections.example: Visualizing a text prompt 'A robot painting a sunset' turning into a pixelated sketch, then a refined image.

sections.title: CLIP: Mapping Language to Visual Space
sections.content: Explain Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP). Concept: Mapping text and image embeddings into a shared high-dimensional vector space using cosine similarity. Prerequisite: Dot products measure alignment.
sections.example: A graph showing an image vector and a text vector pointing in the same direction in 3D space, showing their 'alignment' score.

sections.title: The Diffusion Process: Math as an Artist
sections.content: Introduce Forward Diffusion (adding Gaussian noise) and Reverse Diffusion (denoising). Math concept: Markov Chains. We learn a neural network to predict the noise component ε at each step t.
sections.example: An animation of a clear photo of a 'Golden Retriever' gradually turning into static white noise, then reversing the process.

sections.title: Guidance: Bridging Text and Noise
sections.content: Explain how the CLIP embedding influences the denoising step. We use 'Classifier-Free Guidance' to push the diffusion model to predict noise that aligns better with the text prompt vector.
sections.example: A vector field showing the noise-prediction gradient being 'tilted' or steered by the text input toward the desired image content.

sections.title: Synthesis and Conclusion
sections.content: Summarize the iterative refinement process. The model starts with pure noise and performs 50-100 denoising steps, each steered by CLIP, to arrive at a coherent image.
sections.example: A summary graphic: [Prompt] -> [CLIP Embedding] -> [Denoising Loop] -> [High-Res Image of a Cyberpunk City].
